     Release on the planned date and list the open review findings in the
     release notes. This keeps the schedule and gets users the new features
     fast, but it carries the risk that unfixed defects reach users and need a
     quick patch later.
  2. Fix critical findings, then release this week
     Hold the release a few days to repair only the high-severity review
     findings. Lower-risk items move to the next version. This balances safety
     and speed, but it needs a clear severity cut line and a short retest before
     shipping.
  3. Fix every finding before any release
     Delay the release until all review findings are fixed and verified by a
     full retest. This gives the cleanest build and the least user risk, but it
     moves the date by an unknown amount and delays all new features.
  4. Release gradually to a small user group
     Ship the build to a small share of users first, watch crash and error
     reports, and widen the rollout in steps. This limits the damage from
     unfixed findings, but it needs monitoring, a rollback path, and more total
     release time.
  5. Type something.
